questions.stem: Which type of radiation is used as a medical tracer inside the body?

options.text: Beta, because it is stopped by the skin
Gamma, because it can pass out of the body to be detected externally
All three types are equally suitable
Alpha, because it is the most ionising

questions.explanation: Gamma emitters are used as medical tracers because gamma rays can pass out of the body and be detected by a camera outside. Alpha and beta would be absorbed inside the body and could not be detected externally.

questions.stem: Why should a medical tracer have a short half-life?

options.text: So it can be stored for longer
So it decays quickly and does not remain radioactive in the body for a long time
So it is cheaper to produce
So it produces more radiation

questions.explanation: A short half-life (typically hours) means the tracer decays quickly after the medical procedure, minimising the radiation dose to the patient. It must be long enough to complete the scan but short enough to limit exposure.

questions.stem: Which type of radiation is used in smoke detectors?

options.text: X-rays
Beta
Gamma
Alpha

questions.explanation: Smoke detectors use alpha emitters (such as americium-241). Alpha particles ionise the air, creating a small current. When smoke enters, it absorbs the alpha particles, reducing the current and triggering the alarm.

questions.stem: What three factors must be considered when choosing a radioactive isotope for a particular application?

options.text: Type of radiation emitted, half-life, and whether the source is used inside or outside the body/material
Colour, size, and weight of the isotope
Cost, availability, and country of origin
Temperature, pressure, and density

questions.explanation: The type of radiation (alpha, beta, or gamma), the half-life (how long it remains active), and whether the source is used internally or externally are the three key factors for selecting an appropriate isotope.

questions.stem: Why is gamma radiation used to sterilise medical equipment?

options.text: Because it changes the colour of the equipment
Because it is the cheapest type of radiation
Because it can penetrate packaging and kill bacteria without making the equipment radioactive
Because it heats the equipment to high temperatures

questions.explanation: Gamma rays can penetrate sealed packaging to kill bacteria and viruses. The equipment does not become radioactive (irradiation, not contamination), so it is safe to use immediately after treatment.

questions.stem: Beta radiation is used to monitor the thickness of paper in a factory. Why is beta used rather than alpha or gamma?

options.text: Because beta is partially absorbed by paper, so changes in thickness cause detectable changes in count rate
Because beta radiation is visible
Because beta has the longest half-life
Because beta is the cheapest to produce

questions.explanation: Beta is partially absorbed by paper, so the amount detected on the other side varies with paper thickness. Alpha would be fully absorbed by even thin paper, and gamma would pass through with almost no absorption.

questions.stem: Gamma radiation is used to treat cancer. How does it work?

options.text: It makes the cancer cells radioactive
It damages the DNA of cancer cells, killing them or preventing them from dividing
It dissolves the tumour chemically
It heats the tumour until the cancer cells die

questions.explanation: High-energy gamma rays are focused on the tumour from multiple angles. The radiation damages the DNA of cancer cells, killing them or preventing them from reproducing. Healthy tissue receives a lower dose.
